title: Run credential call
description: The body of the control plane's call with the path run-credential, a POST of application/json to the adapter's call_url followed by run-credential (adapter.schema.json), signed as definitions.schema.json describes a call: an access credential for one run, for the resources, at the access level access, for the purpose purpose, under one grant: for a call whose purpose is harness, the grant grant_ref; for a call whose purpose is work, which has no grant_ref, a grant of the connection connection_id. A call whose purpose is work contains connection_id, the connection of the run's target collection, as the control plane holds it for the run's organisation, which is a live connection of that organisation when the call is sent. The adapter checks that the collection whose ref is the one resource is a live collection under connection_id in its state, and does not look the connection up from the ref. It uses only a grant that the control plane's copy of grants has under connection_id (grants.schema.json: GET /v1/grants and the grant entries of the change feed) that covers the collection and allows the access level access, and never a grant of another connection. It never uses a grant that it keeps only while it sends that grant's report again (grants.schema.json). For a call whose purpose is harness, grant_ref and each resource are as the adapter answered them to a resolve call (resolve-answer.schema.json). A call whose purpose is harness has access read, and the schema refuses any other access for it. The control plane uses a credential from a call whose purpose is harness only with access read, and checks whether a run may use the credential each time it uses the credential for a run, not once when the credential was minted. The rules depend on the call that the credential came from. A credential from a call made for a run of the grant's organisation, under a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation, is used only for runs of that organisation, including a credential under credential_scope grant that covers every resource of the grant. A credential from a call made for an assignment is used only for runs of the organisation of that assignment, and only to read the assigned source. A run that may use a grant only through an assignment uses only a credential of the second kind, from a call made for that assignment, with credential_scope resource and resources set to the resource_ref of the assigned source alone; under credential_scope grant, such a run gets no harness credential and reads the assigned source only with the call with the path read. The adapter answers a signed 200 with run-credential-answer.schema.json, or refuses with refusal.schema.json, in this order: 409 grant_unknown, for a call with grant_ref, the adapter holds no grant grant_ref; 403 resource_not_covered, the grant does not cover one of the resources, or, for a call whose purpose is work, the collection is not a live collection under connection_id in the adapter's state, or no grant of that connection in the control plane's copy of grants covers it; 403 access_not_granted, the grant does not allow access for the resources, such as write under a grant that allows read alone, or, for a call whose purpose is work, a grant of that connection covers the collection and none allows the access level access; 503 source_unavailable, the source did not answer or was busy, and the control plane may send the call again later, built anew. How far one credential reaches is the description's credential_scope (description.schema.json). A call whose purpose is work has exactly one resource in resources, the ref of the collection of the run's target, exactly as the adapter wrote it as ref in its listing of collections (source-collections.schema.json) and as collection_ref in its listing of items (source-items.schema.json); when the run's target came from an item, that collection is the item's collection. That resource is not a resource_ref of a resolve result. A call whose purpose is work has one resource because the answer stays inside the run's work credential entry, whose paths the control plane fills with the path of that one target (run-credential-answer.schema.json); a call whose purpose is harness has 1 to 64. The adapter refuses a call whose time is more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. The adapter has one access key for every organisation, and no call but a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work contains a connection_id, so a resolve result can contain a grant_ref of a connection of another organisation. The control plane uses a resolve result only under a grant that the run may use: a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation; or, only to read a harness source and only with access read, a grant whose organisation assigned that source to the run's organisation, at that version and at that path or export. Under an assignment, the control plane sends a call with the path run-credential only when the credential_scope of the adapter's description is resource, which it also is when absent (description.schema.json), and with resources set to the resource_ref of the assigned source alone; when credential_scope is grant, the control plane sends no call with the path run-credential under an assignment, and reads the assigned source only with the call with the path read. A harness source is a remote source that the run's harness extends or takes a module from, whether that harness is the harness file of the target or the harness member of the run documents (run/v1 documents.schema.json). An assignment never covers a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work or whose access is write: work access comes only from a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation. The control plane treats every other resolve result as covered: false, so nothing that a run of one organisation receives shows that another organisation holds a grant for that address. The control plane sends a call with the path read, and a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is harness, only under a grant that the run may use, and sends a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work only with the connection_id of the run's target collection, which is a live connection of the run's organisation when the call is sent. An access token covers its resources at every version and at every path, so an assignment of one version and one path or export still lets the run read the whole resource with the access token. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The adapter refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the control plane built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The adapter refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

grant_ref.description: The grant the credential is minted under, as the adapter reported it (grant.schema.json). Present exactly when the purpose is harness. A call whose purpose is work has no grant_ref: the adapter uses a grant that the control plane's copy of grants has under connection_id, that covers the collection and allows the access level access, and never a grant of another connection.

connection_id.description: The connection of the run's target collection, as the control plane holds it for the run's organisation (definitions.schema.json, connection_id), which is a live connection of that organisation when the call is sent. Present exactly when the purpose is work. The adapter checks that the collection whose ref is the one resource is a live collection under connection_id in its state, and does not look the connection up from the ref. It uses only a grant that the control plane's copy of grants has under connection_id (grants.schema.json: GET /v1/grants and the grant entries of the change feed) that covers the collection and allows the access level access, and never a grant of another connection. It never uses a grant that it keeps only while it sends that grant's report again (grants.schema.json).

resources.description: The resources the credential covers, none twice. For the purpose harness, 1 to 64, each a resource_ref as the adapter answered it to a resolve call. For the purpose work, exactly one: the ref of the collection of the run's target, exactly as the adapter wrote it as ref in its listing of collections (source-collections.schema.json) and as collection_ref in its listing of items (source-items.schema.json); when the run's target came from an item, that collection is the item's collection.

access.description: read for the purpose harness; read or write for the purpose work: the access level the run has on the resources. For a call whose purpose is work, the access of the run's documents (run/v1 documents.schema.json).

purpose.description: harness, a credential the run uses to fetch what composes its harness; or work, a credential the run uses for its work on the resources.
